entities.name: PMID:10744274
observations: In isolated human PMNs, 180 mM Na+ hypertonic saline given before PAF priming or before fMLP activation reduced beta2-integrin expression, superoxide production, and elastase release; given after activation it increased superoxide and elastase.
Authors concluded that maximal attenuation occurs before priming and post-activation exposure augments cytotoxicity.

entities.name: PMID:10909888
observations: In vitro, hypertonic saline produced transient suppression but could not suppress neutrophils already stimulated with fMLP. In hemorrhaged BALB/c mice, later hypertonic saline after partial lactated Ringer resuscitation caused greater lung damage than early hypertonic saline before lactated Ringer resuscitation (P<0.05).

entities.name: PMID:12095130
observations: In a hemorrhagic-shock mesenteric-lymph model, 7.5% NaCl resuscitation or 180 mM NaCl PMN preincubation before lymph priming inhibited superoxide production, endothelial adherence, and PMN-mediated endothelial cytotoxicity; post-activation treatment was not directly tested.

entities.name: PMID:11331449
observations: In isolated human PMNs, 180 mmol/L Na+ hypertonic saline exposure before PAF/fMLP stimulation suppressed beta2-integrin expression, elastase release, and superoxide production; normotonicity restored responses and repeated hypertonic challenge re-suppressed them.

entities.name: HTS timing effect
observations: Hypertonic saline attenuates PMN cytotoxicity most effectively before priming or activation; after activation it is ineffective or can augment cytotoxic outputs.
Evidence spans isolated human PMNs and a mouse hemorrhagic-shock lung-injury model.
